configKeys.effect: Base fraction of absorbed damage reflected back to the attacker, scaled by the armor's Thorns level (0.0 = none, 1.0 = full). Total reflect is capped at 1.0 (min(1.0, fraction * thornsLevel)).
Snap the wolf's head down when it lands a bite. Also gates the lunge and the server-side bite-direction packet; it does NOT gate the swing-timer mixin.
Restrict the animation to a wolf that is being ridden (off by default, because a dog that only bites visibly while carrying someone looks stranger than one that always does).
Scales how far the head swings and how far the lunge travels; 1.0 is about 50 degrees of head pitch (BITE_PITCH = 0.9 rad).

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.entity.player.PlayerInteractEvent.EntityInteract (game bus) - equip armor by right-click on an owned, tame, non-baby wolf with an empty body slot; remove with any item that can perform ItemAbilities.SHEARS_REMOVE_ARMOR

net.neoforged.neoforge.event.entity.living.LivingDamageEvent.Pre (game bus) - THREE separate handlers: onWolfBiteDirection (sends the bite yaw packet; fires for ANY wolf, armored or not), onWolfHurt (100% absorption + Thorns reflect), onMobDamagedByWolf (Sharpness bonus)

net.neoforged.neoforge.event.entity.living.LivingEquipmentChangeEvent (game bus) - adds/removes the ATTACK_DAMAGE attribute modifier (id vanillaplusadditions:wolf_armor_bonus, ADD_VALUE) on EquipmentSlot.BODY change
net.neoforged.neoforge.event.AddReloadListenerEvent (game bus) - registers the code-only crafting recipes
net.neoforged.neoforge.network.event.RegisterPayloadHandlersEvent (mod bus, registered in onInitialize) - registers WolfBiteDirectionPacket as an OPTIONAL play-to-client channel on registrar "1"
net.neoforged.neoforge.client.event.EntityRenderersEvent.AddLayers (mod bus, @EventBusSubscriber(Dist.CLIENT, MOD)) - adds BattleDogsArmorLayer to the wolf renderer; NOT gated on isModuleEnabled()

net.neoforged.neoforge.client.event.RenderLivingEvent.Pre (priority LOWEST) and RenderLivingEvent.Post (priority HIGHEST) (@EventBusSubscriber(Dist.CLIENT, GAME)) - the bite lunge push/pop on the PoseStack
mixins: battle_dogs.WolfSwingTimeMixin (both sides - listed in the "mixins" block of vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json; @Inject at HEAD of Wolf.aiStep, drives swingTime/attackAnim the way Monster.aiStep does)
battle_dogs.WolfBiteAnimationMixin (client - listed in the "client" block; @Inject at TAIL of WolfModel.setupAnim, adds head.xRot and upperBody.xRot)
notes:
PROVABLE FACTS A DOC WRITER NEEDS

Tier table (WolfArmorItem.Tier, durability / flat attack bonus): IRON 200 / +1.0, GOLD 100 / +2.0, DIAMOND 400 / +3.0, NETHERITE 600 / +4.0. Netherite is the only fire-resistant one (`new Item.Properties().fireResistant()` at BattleDogsModule:77). Gold is the deliberate odd one out: second-highest attack bonus on the LOWEST durability. All four use vanilla `ArmorMaterials.ARMADILLO` with `BodyType.CANINE` and `hasOverlay = false` (item/WolfArmorItem.java:43 - the third `AnimalArmorItem` argument is `hasOverlay`, which controls the dyeable `_overlay.png` layer; armour trims are not part of `AnimalArmorItem` in 1.21.1), so the repair ingredient is the armadillo scute.

Combat mechanics, exactly as coded:
- Absorption (onWolfHurt, BattleDogsModule:298): the armor eats 100% of the damage (`event.setNewDamage(0f)`) and pays `max(1, ceil(absorbed))` durability. The handler checks ONLY "entity is a Wolf" and "body armor is a WolfArmorItem" - it does not check tame or owner, so any wolf wearing this armor (e.g. placed via /item) is effectively invulnerable until it breaks.
- Thorns: read off the stack BEFORE hurtAndBreak so a breaking piece still reflects. Reflect amount = absorbed * min(1.0, thorns_reflect_fraction * thornsLevel) via `MobArmorEnchantments.reflectThorns`; server-side only, skipped when the source's *indirect* entity (`source.getEntity()`) is not a living, still-alive entity or is the wolf itself.
- Sharpness (onMobDamagedByWolf, BattleDogsModule:331): +0.5 + 0.5 * level added to outgoing damage, only when the wolf wears OUR armor. Both direct and indirect source entity are checked; a Wolf as victim is skipped so the two handlers never overlap.
- Unbreaking is not handled in code at all - it works natively through vanilla `hurtAndBreak` (see MobArmorEnchantments' class javadoc).
- The armor is enchantable because `src/main/resources/data/minecraft/tags/item/enchantable/{armor,durability,sharp_weapon}.json` add the four wolf items (shared files with the cat/axolotl armors; sharp_weapon holds no flying_fish_boots).

Equipping (onPlayerInteractEntity, BattleDogsModule:160): both branches require `wolf.isTame() && wolf.isOwnedBy(player)`. Equipping additionally needs an empty body slot and `!wolf.isBaby()`; removal does NOT check isBaby, only that the held item can perform `ItemAbilities.SHEARS_REMOVE_ARMOR`. The removed armor is dropped on the ground (`spawnAtLocation`), NOT returned to the inventory, and the shears take 1 durability. Creative players do not lose the armor stack when equipping.

Recipes are code-only (per the repo convention): injected in `applyBattleDogsRecipes` through a `PreparableReloadListener` added on `AddReloadListenerEvent`, gated on isModuleEnabled(). Shape is "S  " / "XXX" / "X X" with S = armadillo scute and X = the tier material, CraftingBookCategory.EQUIPMENT. The original JSON recipe files (added in cc0ba0c under the pre-1.21 plural folder `data/vanillaplusadditions/recipes/`) were deleted in 118f9fd - do not document a datapack path; `src/main/resources/data` has no recipe folder at all today.

Items are registered by a DeferredRegister that is attached to the mod bus inside `onInitialize` (BattleDogsModule:93), and `ModuleManager.initializeModules` only initializes modules the config enables. Disabling the module therefore means the four items do not exist in the registry at all.

KNOWN LIMITS / GOTCHAS

1. STANDALONE JAR IS CRIPPLED. `build.gradle:395` is the bare entry `[ moduleId: 'battle_dogs', displayName: 'Vanilla Plus: Battle Dogs' ]` - no `mixins:`, no `clientMixins:`, no `dataGlobs:`. Consequences, both provable from the packaging tasks (build.gradle 466-476 descriptor defaults, 579-600 generateMeta, 628-660 moduleJar): (a) `vpa_battle_dogs.jar` ships neither WolfSwingTimeMixin nor WolfBiteAnimationMixin and no `vpa_battle_dogs.mixins.json` (the only mixin vpa_core carries is `core.EntitySharedFlagInvoker`, build.gradle:535), so in standalone mode `attackAnim` stays pinned at 0 and BOTH the head snap and the WolfBiteLunge (which reads `getAttackAnim`) are dead, even though the bite_animation config keys still exist; (b) the enchantable tag JSONs are not included (cat_guardian and axolotl_guardian at least list armor.json + durability.json in their dataGlobs - note that none of the three ships sharp_weapon.json) so wolf armor cannot be enchanted from a standalone jar. Textures/models are unaffected: `coreJar` ships all of `assets/vanillaplusadditions/**`. Everything here is provable from build.gradle alone; no jar was built to confirm.

2. README CONTRADICTION. `README.md:33` says the armor is "rendered by the vanilla wolf-armor layer". The module actually registers its OWN `BattleDogsArmorLayer` onto the wolf renderer in `BattleDogsClientSetup.onAddLayers`, which bakes `ModelLayers.WOLF_ARMOR` into a second WolfModel and draws the item's own `getTexture()`. The crackiness overlays it draws on top ARE vanilla textures (`ResourceLocation.withDefaultNamespace("textures/entity/wolf/wolf_armor_crackiness_*.png")`), the armor texture is the mod's own (`vanillaplusadditions:textures/entity/wolf/wolf_armor_<tier>.png`). Whether vanilla's WolfArmorLayer ALSO renders these items - they are AnimalArmorItem/CANINE - cannot be proven from this repo, since vanilla sources are not checked in and no decompiled sources are available locally. Flagged as unverified rather than guessed.

3. STALE CONFIG JAVADOC. The class javadoc of `BattleDogsConfig` claims it adds "the shared mob-armor combat-effect keys (default Unbreaking/Sharpness/Thorns levels and the thorns reflect fraction)". `buildModuleSpecificConfig` defines only `thorns_reflect_fraction` plus the three `bite_animation` keys - there are no default-enchantment-level keys in this module. Do not document any.

4. CLIENT SETUP IS NOT GATED, BUT IT CANNOT MISFIRE. `BattleDogsClientSetup` is a plain `@EventBusSubscriber(Dist.CLIENT, MOD)` with no isModuleEnabled() check, so the render layer is added to the wolf renderer even when the module is disabled. It is inert: with the module disabled `onInitialize` never runs, the DeferredRegister is never attached, no WolfArmorItem instance can exist, and the layer's `instanceof WolfArmorItem` early-return always fires. (Disabling the module does NOT leave armor rendered on wolves - it removes the items from the registry entirely, which is the real consequence worth documenting: existing stacks/equipped armor become unknown items.)

5. SWING TIMER RUNS EVEN WITH THE ANIMATION OFF. `WolfSwingTimeMixin` checks only `isModuleActive()`, not `isBiteAnimation()`. With `bite_animation.enabled = false` the wolf's swingTime/attackAnim are still maintained every tick, on both sides. That is arguably intentional (the mixin's javadoc explains that untended, the very first `swing()` latches the `swinging` flag and every later bite stops broadcasting its ClientboundAnimatePacket) - but it does mean the module changes vanilla wolf state even in its "animation off" configuration.

6. SERVER-CRASH HISTORY ON THE PACKET. The bite-direction channel is registered `optional()`, which only saves the handshake. Sending still had to be gated per player with `player.connection.hasChannel(...)`, because `NetworkRegistry.checkPacket` throws inside `Wolf.aiStep` - a ticking-entity crash. Per CHANGELOG.md 125-147 (`## [1.0.0-beta.81] - 2026-09-18`) this crash-looped games2 on 2026-09-18 with one player on an older build; the bug had been in since beta.76 and the documented stop-gap at the time was `[modules.battle_dogs.bite_animation] enabled = false`. Tracking is approximated by `EntityType.clientTrackingRange() * 16` rather than reading ChunkMap - a player just outside real tracking range loses one packet.

7. `BiteDirections` NEVER EVICTS. Entries in the static `ConcurrentHashMap<Integer, long[]>` expire logically after 500 ms but are never removed; the map keeps one entry per distinct wolf entity id that ever bit near the player. The javadoc calls this out as deliberate ("a stale entry is simply never read again"), but strictly it grows for the lifetime of the client session.

8. TWO ANIMATIONS ON PURPOSE. The head snap (mixin, `head.xRot` += curve*0.9*strength, `upperBody.xRot` += curve*0.12*strength) is the nicer motion but is overwritten by Entity Model Features + Fresh Animations, which re-applies `wolf.jem` part rotations AFTER `setupAnim` returns. `WolfBiteLunge` exists as the version that survives that, working on the render pose (0.32 blocks forward, 0.10 down at full swing). It is a translation, not a rotation, deliberately (a rotation there would land in world space, before `setupRotations`). The offset scales with `wolf.getScale()`, so a 3.25-scale `wolf_mount` lunges proportionally. Both read the same `attackAnim` ramp and honour enabled / only_when_ridden / strength.

9. DEBUG LATCHES. Both mixins carry a one-shot static `announced` boolean that logs via `BattleDogsModule.debug(...)` only when `debug_logging` is on. They fire once per JVM, not once per wolf - a doc writer should not promise repeated diagnostics.

10. COUPLING WITH wolf_mount (one-way, by design). `wolf_mount` deliberately never imports a battle_dogs class: `WolfMountRules:39-40` tests `instanceof AnimalArmorItem` with `BodyType.CANINE`, and `WolfMountArmorHud:222` matches by item-id path heuristic. So wolf_mount works with battle_dogs absent, but its armor HUD is the natural companion to this module. Ordering nuance, per docs/modules/wolf_mount.md:265-270: wolf_mount's rider immunity cancels on `LivingIncomingDamageEvent`, which fires well BEFORE `LivingDamageEvent.Pre` (the event all three battle_dogs damage handlers use), so on that path `onWolfHurt` is simply never reached.

11. JEI IS NOT DECLARED IN neoforge.mods.toml. The bundle's mods.toml lists optional deps for create, toughasnails, sable and bluemap - there is no `jei` entry. JEI integration works purely because `@JeiPlugin` classes are loaded by JEI's own annotation scan and JEI is `compileOnly` (build.gradle:110-113, full JEI only at localRuntime:113). The `isModuleEnabled("battle_dogs")` gate at BattleDogsJeiPlugin:34 also guards the four `DeferredItem.get()` calls below it, which would throw when the module never initialized.

12. Localisation: item names exist in all six lang files (en_us, de_de, de_at, fr_fr, es_es, cs_cz), four keys each. The two tooltip lines are shared with the cat/axolotl armors under `tooltip.vanillaplusadditions.mob_armor.attack` / `.absorb` (via `util/MobArmorTooltip`, which lives in util so vpa_core carries it), so editing them affects three modules.

13. History, corrected: `cc0ba0c` (2026-06-12 04:51) is a genuine add (status A) of the module directory - BattleDogsModule, BattleDogsArmorLayer, BattleDogsClientSetup, WolfArmorItem, plus the four (now deleted) recipe JSONs - and it is the OLDEST commit touching the module, also under `git log --follow`. The same-day commits `265c3e9` "Alpha 1" (05:12, introduced `applyBattleDogsRecipes`) and `e642ca0` "Alpha 1: Implement 100% damage absorption for Wolf Armor" (14:06) come AFTER it, not before; there is no earlier path for WolfArmorItem anywhere in history, so the code does not predate the module layout. All three are contained in v1.0.0-beta (`git describe --contains cc0ba0c` = `v1.0.0-beta~15`). The bite animation is much younger: `cb19a38` (2026-09-08, `v1.0.0-beta.76~1`) added WolfBiteLunge, BiteDirections, WolfBiteDirectionPacket and both mixins.

14. The four items are added to the mod's main creative tab via `VanillaPlusCreativeTabs.addAllToMainTab` (BattleDogsModule:95-96); there is no battle_dogs-specific tab.

No commands, keybinds, blocks or entities (the module's only DeferredRegister is `DeferredRegister.createItems`, BattleDogsModule:58-59). No TODO/FIXME comments in the module or its mixins (the only grep hit for "XXX" is the recipe pattern string "X X"/"XXX"). There is no docs/modules/battle_dogs.md yet.
oneLiner: Tamed wolves can wear iron, gold, diamond or netherite body armor that soaks up every point of incoming damage until it breaks, makes the wolf hit noticeably harder, and finally gives a biting wolf a visible head-snap and lunge instead of vanilla's motionless attack.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: BattleDogsJeiPlugin (loaded only by JEI's own annotation scan, gated on ModuleManager.isModuleEnabled("battle_dogs")) shows the four wolf armors' armadillo-scute anvil repairs (JeiMobArmorRepairs) and their possible enchantments (JeiMobArmorEnchantments) in JEI. Without JEI nothing breaks - the repairs and enchantments still work in an anvil, they are just undiscoverable in a recipe viewer, because vanilla anvil repair is code-only and JEI's anvil list is hardcoded vanilla.

vanillaplusadditions:wolf_armor_gold - same pattern with X = minecraft:gold_ingot
vanillaplusadditions:wolf_armor_diamond - same pattern with X = minecraft:diamond
vanillaplusadditions:wolf_armor_netherite - same pattern with X = minecraft:netherite_ingot

shortDescription: Adds iron, gold, diamond, and netherite armor for tamed wolves.
